title: PR 4821 review notes - kv cache & batching refactor
content:
Quick scratchpad for PR 4821 (kv-cache + batching refactor) — mostly TODOs and comments I plan to post.

High-level summary:
- Consolidates kv cache logic from runtime/cache/* into runtime/kv_cache (single interface)
- Introduces continuous batching shim that integrates with new cache API
- Changes cache key format (adds context hash + model version) to reduce collisions
- Adds an in-memory LRU with async persistence hooks (WIP)

My top concerns / sanity checks:
- Correctness: cache key change backwards compatibility? need migration plan for deduped entries (see note below).
- Concurrency: new LRU uses lock per-shard but batch hotpath still does a global await on disk-persist hook — could increase tail latency under sudden churn. Try to avoid blocking hotpath.
- Eviction policy: default TTL vs size-based eviction — what are sensible defaults for hosted API vs dedicated? add config flags.

Local repro / perf runs to validate:
- Run microbench: ./scripts/bench_kv_cache.sh --model gpt-3.5 --seq 512 --q 1000
- Use profiler: python -m pyinstrument serving_runtime/main.py --bench --profile=kv --output=prof.html
- CI: there are two flaky tests in cache_test.py (test_persist_async and test_eviction_order) — failures reproducible locally with env CACHE_PERSIST=1

Suggested review checklist (what I'm going to comment inline):
- [ ] API surface: Is new KVCache trait small and stable? (methods: get, set, prefetch, invalidate, stats)
- [ ] Backwards compatibility: Are old keys still readable? if not, document migration + header/versioning on keys.
- [ ] Benchmarks: include tail latency (p95/p99) numbers before/after on dedicated instance type (a10g?). Ask infra to run 1h soak.
- [ ] Tests: unit + integration (end-to-end serving with cache warmup) — add a smoke test that simulates model version rollover.
- [ ] Error handling: persistence hook failures should not cause request failures. Log+metrics only.
- [ ] Observability: add cache hit/miss counters, eviction counts, average latency per op — wire into console telemetry.
- [ ] Docs: update README + migration guide + config reference (default TTL, shard count, persist mode).

Refactor suggestions (non-blocking, but preferable):
- Split the big file runtime/kv_cache/manager.go into manager + sharding + persistence modules. Current file is 1.6k LOC — hard to review.
- Extract async persistence into a worker pool with bounded queue and backpressure metrics. Right now it spawns a goroutine per write which can amplify memory pressure.
- Replace ad-hoc locking with a small syncmap + per-shard mutexes to reduce contention on get/set hotpath.
- Consider using the existing serialized prefix cache code (runtime/cache/prefix_cache.go) for common prefix handling instead of reimplementing.

Follow-ups (create issues if merged):
- Add canary rollout config that pins keys to model version and falls back to older key format for N minutes. (JIRA-RT-2045)
- Add a maintenance job to coalesce/pause persistence during large GC windows.
- Investigate swapping LRU to CLOCK if eviction profiling shows high churn CPU.

Inline notes / things to ask the author (I will paste into PR comments):
- L18-22: Why include model version in key rather than using header? Authors: provide rationale, potential impact on cache hit rate.
- L78: Is the global persistWaitGroup necessary? causes blocking in shutdown path — suggest converting to context-aware cancellation + graceful drain.
- L134-150: Unit tests rely on time.Sleep(100ms) to wait for async persistence. Replace with sync hooks or test-only WaitGroup to make tests deterministic.
- L212: Magic number 4096 for shard count — suggest configurable and add explanation comment (hash distribution expected).

Draft comments to post (short snippets):
- "Can you add a migration plan for the key format change? even a one-paragraph note in the PR description is fine."
- "Prefer bounded worker pool for persistence rather than goroutine-per-write — risk of unbounded growth under load."
- "Some of the large helper functions could be split for easier unit testing (e.g., key serialization + hash)."

Quick TODOs for me if this lands:
- Add perf dashboard in console under: "kv-cache / PR-4821" with hit/miss and p50/p95/p99 latency.
- Coordinate with infra for dedicated soak: ping @infra-ops with run specs and budget.
- Add migration guide to confluence page referenced above.

Random notes / brain dump (ignore):
- If we want cold-start reduction, consider warming on first request for a model-version combo using short-lived prefetch window.
- Might be useful to add a TTL jitter to avoid stampeding (randomize +/- 10%).

End of scratchpad. Re-check tests locally before posting.
